title: Agent Control Clone Governance After Control Edits
dataSources: The list of controls attached to each Agent Stream compared with the team's control definitions
description: Keeps attached controls in step with their originals. Attaching a control to an Agent Stream clones it, and editing the original does not update the clone, so a fix can miss the streams it was meant for.
value: A tightened pattern that never reaches production leaves the gap open while the team believes it is closed. Tracking clones per stream closes that blind spot.
implementation: Keep each control definition in version control with the streams it should be attached to. After editing a control, update or re-attach the clone on every listed stream, then compare the attached control with the definition.
visualization: Per-stream checklist of attached controls and the definition version each matches.

references.title: Splunk Agent Observability: Agent Control overview

knownFalsePositives: Streams that intentionally run a different version of a control (for example during an observe rollout) show as different; record the exception.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites

A Splunk Agent Observability project for the application and one Agent Stream per environment or agent inside it. Do not create a second project for the same application: a second project splits the traces. The agent reads `SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT` and `SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM` from the environment. SaaS tenants authenticate with `SPLUNK_AO_REALM` and `SPLUNK_AO_O11Y_TOKEN`; on-prem tenants with `SPLUNK_AO_API_KEY` plus `SPLUNK_AO_CONSOLE_URL`. Install the SDK with `pip install splunk-ao` (`pip install "splunk-ao[langchain]"` for the LangChain callback). Agent Control is a separate server and a separate install (`agent-control-sdk`, plus `agent-control-evaluators`; one of those packages is still named `agent-control-evaluator-galileo`, the platform's old name).

Step 1 — Instrument the agent

The app calls `agent_control.init` and decorates the step with `@control(step_name=...)`. There are two ways to bind a control, and a tenant uses one of them. The Splunk Agent Observability docs pass the resolved `agent_stream_id` (not the stream name) as `target_id` and attach the control to the stream in the console. The SDK path calls `init(agent_name=...)`, creates a policy, adds the control to it, and assigns the policy to that agent name. If the repo already has an example, follow it. Run the decorated step inside an open trace so the control span lands on that trace.

Step 2 — Configure in Splunk Agent Observability

A control has a scope (step type `llm` or `tool`, step name, and stage `pre` or `post`), a condition (a selector path such as `input` or `output` plus a check from the control server's catalog: regex, list, JSON, SQL, Luna-2 or custom), and an action. Actions, strictest first: deny, steer, observe; deny wins over steer over observe. Regex patterns are RE2, so there is no lookahead. Write the pattern as the thing to catch: the engine has no "unless".

Step 3 — Validate

Edit an original control on a test project and confirm the attached clone did not change, so the team sees the behaviour. This use case was written from the Splunk Agent Observability documentation without access to a tenant, so it ships as a draft. Confirm each step in the Splunk Agent Observability console before promoting it.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add the clone update to the change checklist for every control edit.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

A fix did not take effect: the clone on the stream still has the old pattern.
grandmaExplanation: When we change a rule, we check every copy of it that was handed out, because the copies do not update themselves.

productArtifacts.title: Clone update procedure
productArtifacts.body:
Fact: attaching a control to a stream clones it. Editing the original does not update the clone. The clone applies without a redeploy.
1. Edit the control definition in version control.
2. For each stream listed with the control, update or re-attach the clone.
3. Compare each stream's attached control with the definition.
4. Record the streams updated.
